salient_findings: Mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall
No prior medical history or symptoms
key_facts: 42-year-old man
Underwent transthoracic echocardiography as part of a routine medical checkup
Left ventricular mass revealed on echocardiography
No prior medical history
Denied fever, weight loss, dyspnea, or other symptoms
Temperature 36.5 °C on admission
Blood pressure 120/80 mm Hg on admission
Electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm
Chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Mass measured 1.34 × 1.9 cm on echocardiography
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed focal contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Left ventricular myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common primary cardiac tumor, matches description of mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass

shortlist.label: Papillary fibroelastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Second most common primary cardiac tumor, can appear as a small, mobile, pedunculated mass

shortlist.label: Thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of left ventricular mass, especially if patient has a history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac conditions

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, benign cardiac tumor that can appear as a mass in the left ventricle

shortlist.label: Metastatic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, metastatic disease can present as a cardiac mass, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The mass is described as a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass, which is consistent with the typical appearance of a left ventricular myxoma. The presence of focal contrast enhancement on computed tomography also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Papillary fibroelastoma
rejected.why: Papillary fibroelastomas are typically smaller and more often found on the valves

rejected.label: Thrombus
rejected.why: The mass's description as smooth and pedunculated, along with the lack of symptoms or history suggesting thrombosis, makes thrombus less likely

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: Fibromas are typically found in the ventricular septum and are less likely to be pedunculated or show focal contrast enhancement

rejected.label: Metastatic tumor
rejected.why: There is no prior medical history or symptoms suggesting cancer, making metastatic tumor less likely
